Load a selection cascade (system > module > gene > probe)

Source: R/cascade_sets.R
dmsa_sets.Rd

The cascade declares the analysis structure DMSA corrects within. Loading it is separate from loading a direction map: the cascade says which probes form which unit, the direction map says which way each probe points.

Usage

dmsa_sets(x = "alpha", audit = NULL, polarity = NULL, name = NULL)

Arguments

x

Either "alpha" for the bundled, literature-audited Project Alpha 2026c cascade, a path to a CSV (optionally .gz) in the same shape, or a data.frame already in that shape. See dmsa_sets_template() for the schema and dmsa_sets_check() to validate a file before use.

audit

Optional module-level evidence table: a path or data.frame with one row per module_id and any of evidence_strength, audit_status, citation_keys, evidence_note, deep_search_url. Defaults to the bundled audit when x = "alpha", and to NULL otherwise. When a user cascade already carries these columns they are used and no separate table is needed.

polarity

Optional gene-to-system polarity table (path, data.frame or dmsa_polarity) supplying w_g. Defaults to the bundled Alpha polarity when x = "alpha", to the cascade's own w_g column when it has one, and otherwise to none - in which case a system-level score weights every gene +1 and the print method says so. Use dmsa_polarity_fetch() to draft one for your own panel from public databases.

name

Optional label, printed and carried into reports.

Value

An object of class dmsa_sets.

See also

dmsa_systems() for the short names, dmsa_select() to choose systems, dmsa_evidence() for the module evidence table.

Examples

# \donttest{
cas <- dmsa_sets()          # bundled Alpha 2026c
cas
#> dmsa selection cascade: Project Alpha 2026c (module-audited)
